title: Cache-Hit-Rate Predictor Bundle (per-kernel-per-launch)
description: One bundle per (slug, shape_point, binary_sha256, source_commit, kernel_signature_sha256) tuple. Carries an analytical prediction of the cache hit rate computed by Smith-Eklund LRU stack-distance integration over per-launch reuse-distance evidence recomputed from the producer-side sector_stream/*.jsonl records. The predictor's input MUST be raw reuse-distance evidence (recomputed via tools/hrd_profiler/reuse_distance_tracker.py from sector_stream), NOT the HRD profiler's already-modeled hit_count / hit_rate fields. The non-circular discipline is enforced by the input_sidecar_digests field which lists sector_stream and rejects hrd_profile. One of three result arms (scalar / bounded / typed_unavailable) is emitted depending on bin coverage. The bundle carries the sibling-sidecar manifest_pairing_index shape so verify_artifacts.py binds cached run-summary fields to on-disk bundle provenance the same way the divergence_proxies / sharing_locality / order_projections / perturbation_run_ledger / trace_convergence_confidence sidecars do.

schema_version.description: Bundle schema major version. A deliberate schema bump must update both this constant and consumers in lockstep.

algorithm_version.description: Algorithm identifier for the predictor. Initial value is 'smith_eklund_lru_v1' for the canonical fully-associative LRU stack-distance integration. Bumped when the analytical model changes (e.g., bounded-associativity refinement gated by the ablation ladder documented in plans/cache_hit_rate_predictor_first_plan.md).

arch.description: Optional explicit arch marker. Producer-side additive extension introduced by the sm_120-only activation bundle producer (tools/local_labels/sm120_activation_bundle_producer.py) so the calibration-head fitter's strict-arch verification guard can reject cross-arch joins without falling back to device-string parsing. NOT part of the five-field identity tuple consumed by verify_artifacts.py's manifest_pairing_index cross-check; carried purely as an audit / decoupling marker. Legacy bundles emitted before this field landed continue to validate (field is OPTIONAL) and the fitter falls back to its device-string resolver.

manifest_pairing_index.description: Five-field provenance binding (slug, shape_point, binary_sha256, source_commit, kernel_signature_sha256). The verifier cross-checks every required field against the enclosing run summary to reject a bundle copied from a different binary / kernel / source_commit (per the R4 divergence_proxies widening at d2ec483). An OPTIONAL sixth `arch` audit field may also appear (additive sm_120-only-producer extension); it is NOT joined on by the verifier's five-field cross-check.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the sector_stream sidecar consumed (e.g. trace_<shape>/sector_stream/sector_stream.jsonl).

dynamic_trace_pb.description: Optional cross-check digest of the raw NVBit dynamic_trace.pb.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the launch-parameter sidecar consumed (e.g. data/local_labels/launch_parameters_sidecars/sm_86/launch_parameters_sidecar_<slug>__<shape_point>.json). The sidecar carries the per-cell grid_dim used by the predictor's gridDim density correction; the sidecar is loaded only after its embedded identity tuple (arch / slug / shape_point / binary_sha256 / kernel_signature_sha256) is validated against the caller's admitted-row / manifest tuple, so a stale or swapped sidecar fails closed with typed launch_parameters_sidecar_identity_mismatch rather than silently applying the wrong correction.

launch_parameters_sidecar.description: Optional digest of the per-cell launch-parameter sidecar when the bundle's predicted_hit_rate incorporates the gridDim density correction. The non-leakage discipline applies: only the sidecar's identity fields and grid_dim are read by the loader; label / truth fields (hit_rate, ncu_truth_*, etc.) are NEVER inspected.

input_sidecar_digests.description: Per-input sidecar SHA-256 digests. The non-circular discipline requires sector_stream to be present and forbids hrd_profile from appearing here. The verifier rejects any bundle whose input_sidecar_digests includes hrd_profile / hit_count / hit_rate keys with typed circular_predictor_input_rejected.

device.description: Device name (e.g., 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU' or 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti'). Per-arch covariate; used by the cross-arch transfer-learning evaluation when admitted on both arches.

cache_model_capacity_bytes.description: Cache capacity in bytes used for the Smith-Eklund modeled-hit rule (rd_in_sector_units < capacity_bytes // sector_size_bytes). Sourced from the run summary's l2_cache_size_bytes (CUDA device prop). Per-arch covariate (sm_120 = 33554432; sm_86 = 6291456).

cache_model_num_l2_slices.description: Slice-aware L2 cache geometry. Each sector maps to slice `sector_id % num_l2_slices`; each slice carries `capacity_bytes // num_l2_slices // 32` sectors. 1 = fully-associative pool (back-compat default when no slice geometry is sourced). On sm_86 (GA102 / RTX 3090 Ti) the documented value is 6 (6 MiB L2 split across 6 slices of 1 MiB each). Per-bundle provenance for the slice-geometry assumption Codex's R12 review required.

cache_model_num_l2_slices_source.description: Provenance label for the `cache_model_num_l2_slices` field. Fail-closed to the documented vocabulary so a typo or label drift is rejected at the schema boundary. `constant` = back-compat default 1; `caller_supplied` = caller explicitly passed a non-default value without a more specific provenance; `static_device_card` = sourced from the static device-card fallback table in run_suite.py or the orchestrator; `cuda_device_prop` = sourced from a live CUDA driver attribute (reserved for the future when a CUDA attribute for L2 slice count becomes available); `device_properties_manifest` = sourced from `tools/hrd_profiler/device_properties.json` via `device_properties.resolve_entry(...)`, used by the local-label producer when emitting bundles whose `cache_model_geometry_provenance` block names the same manifest entry; `typed_unavailable` = a refusal arm.

cache_model_cta_interleave_enabled.description: Coarse CTA/SM interleaving flag. When true, the HRD walker round-robin-merges per-threadblock access sequences before walking the LRU stack so reuse distances reflect concurrent-CTA L2 contention. When false (the default for back-compat), the walker preserves the legacy sequential per-TB walk. The headline orchestrator sets this to true on sm_86. Additive widening, no schema_version bump per the wire-extension policy.

cache_model_hrd_second_layer_enabled.description: Maeda 2017 second HRD sector-layer flag. When true, the walker applies a flat first-layer sector tracker check (against capacity_bytes // 32) AND the existing per-slice second-layer tracker check (against capacity_bytes // num_l2_slices // 32); hit = both. When false (the default), the walker preserves the legacy per-slice-only check byte-for-byte. Additive widening per the wire-extension policy. Optional on the legacy bundle-set; a follow-up recapture round flips it true once device-properties provenance is populated on every emitted bundle.

cache_model_cross_launch_state_carryover.description: Cross-launch L2 state carryover flag. When true, the HRD walker carries the surviving sector-LRU state from launch N into launch N+1 within the same (device, stream); the second-and-later launches start warm rather than cold. When false (the default for back-compat), each launch starts cold, byte-for-byte equivalent to the pre-carryover walker. Additive widening per the wire-extension policy. Independent provenance evidence is carried in `evidence.cross_launch_state_carryover_applied_launch_count`: when this flag is true the bundle MUST have `evidence.launch_count >= 2` AND `evidence.cross_launch_state_carryover_applied_launch_count >= 1` for the bundle-provenance scanner at `tools/sm_86_predictor_accuracy_recovery/test_bundle_provenance_scanner.py` to admit it.

cache_model_geometry_provenance.description: Device-properties manifest provenance. Sourced from tools/hrd_profiler/device_properties.json by the 5-tuple (arch, sku, driver_version, cuda_toolkit_version, nvbit_build); manifest_sha256 binds the bundle to the exact manifest bytes. Optional on the legacy bundle-set; a follow-up recapture round populates it on every newly-emitted bundle. The cache_model_geometry_provenance_scanner test enforces cross-checks (capacity match; slice count match; non-placeholder source labels; top-level-vs-provenance agreement on num_l2_slices and cta_interleave).

predictor_build_commit.description: Optional top-level audit anchor: full 40-hex SHA of the producer-code build that emitted the bundle. The headline orchestrator (`tools/local_labels/run_headline_cohort_predict_compare.py`) attaches this field to every bundle it writes so the regeneration_delta scanner can enforce the HEAD-or-HEAD^ accept-set rule. Unit-level callers of `predict_cache_hit_rate` need not set the field; it is optional on the schema (not in `required`).

cache_model_grid_volume.description: Optional top-level audit anchor: the launch's `grid_dim.x * grid_dim.y * grid_dim.z` product, sourced predictor-side from the committed launch-parameter sidecars under `data/local_labels/launch_parameters_sidecars/<arch>/` (NEVER from labels/truth). Drives the gridDim-density correction in the L2 head (penalty proportional to `log2(max(1, grid_volume / sm_count_threshold))`). Absent when `grid_dim` is not supplied by the caller; the predictor's evidence block records the correction's parameters (`grid_dim_input`, `grid_dim_correction_penalty`, `grid_dim_correction_alpha`) regardless.

grid_dim_alpha_source.description: Optional cross-arch extrapolation provenance for the gridDim density penalty alpha (`grid_dim_correction_alpha` in the evidence block). The legacy alpha value 0.110 is empirically calibrated on sm_86 (RTX 3090 Ti) via the activation-cohort tuning; this tag surfaces whether that value is calibrated for the device the bundle was emitted against (`sm_86_calibrated`) or reused cross-arch as a deliberate extrapolation (`sm_86_extrapolated`; emitted on the RTX 5060 Laptop GPU under the legacy cross-arch reuse policy). `sm120_uncalibrated` is emitted on the RTX 5060 Laptop GPU under the sm_120-only decoupled-framework policy, which disables the gridDim-alpha penalty entirely (alpha = 0.0) until a future sm_120-side calibration-evaluation loop replaces this tag with `sm_120_calibrated`. `uncalibrated` is emitted for unknown / unrecognized devices where neither calibrated nor extrapolated semantics apply. Field is OPTIONAL: legacy bundles emitted before this field landed continue to validate. The comparison runner reads but does NOT gate admission on this field (metadata-only).

sector_size_bytes.description: Sector granularity in bytes. Pinned at 32 across all current arches (sm_86 + sm_120) per the existing cache_model_spec discipline.

bootstrap_resamples.description: Bootstrap resampling count. Pinned at 2000 to match the HRD profiler's BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES constant for cross-sidecar consistency.

bootstrap_seed.description: Per-bundle bootstrap seed. Pinning the seed makes the bootstrap CI reproducible across re-runs of the same input; seed drift is detected by the geomean reproducibility check.

epsilon.description: Epsilon floor for the relative-error denominator in the comparison contract. Pinned at 0.01 by default to handle hit rates near 0 / 1 without destabilizing relative error. The bundle carries epsilon for downstream-runner consistency.

result_kind.description: One of three result arms. 'scalar' when bundle_underconfigured=false and a point estimate is admitted. 'bounded' when bundle_underconfigured=true but at least one bin admits (hit_rate_lower / hit_rate_upper bracket the typed-unavailable bins as misses-vs-hits). 'typed_unavailable' when no bin admits (bundle is fully unusable; only typed_reason is meaningful).

predicted_hit_rate.description: Scalar hit-rate prediction in [0, 1]. Required when result_kind == 'scalar'.

ci_low.description: Bootstrap CI lower bound. Required when result_kind == 'scalar'.

ci_high.description: Bootstrap CI upper bound. Required when result_kind == 'scalar'.

ci_half_width.description: (ci_high - ci_low) / 2. Required when result_kind == 'scalar'. The predictor self-consistency metric reportable even before NCU labels admit.

ci_confidence.description: Bootstrap CI confidence level. Pinned at 0.95 for cross-sidecar consistency with the HRD profiler.

hit_rate_lower.description: Bounded interval lower bound: typed-unavailable bins counted as misses. Required when result_kind == 'bounded'.

hit_rate_upper.description: Bounded interval upper bound: typed-unavailable bins counted as hits. Required when result_kind == 'bounded'. Must satisfy hit_rate_lower <= hit_rate_upper.

underconfigured_bin_count.description: Number of reuse-distance bins below the minimum_bin_sample_count threshold. Required when result_kind == 'bounded' or 'typed_unavailable'.

admitted_bin_count.description: Number of reuse-distance bins clearing the minimum_bin_sample_count threshold. Required when result_kind == 'bounded' or 'typed_unavailable'.

typed_reason.description: Typed reason for the predictor's failure to admit. Required when result_kind == 'typed_unavailable'. The enum is the complete set of admit-failure reasons; bumping the enum requires a coordinated update to the verifier and the test surface (BL-20260507 arch-token-multi-surface-lockstep equivalent for typed-reason vocabularies). The `calibration_variance_precondition_failed` reason fires when the cross-cell prediction stddev falls below the documented 0.10 floor, indicating the cohort lacks sufficient variance for the calibration head to fit without overfitting; the predictor's variance-precondition gate (additive kwarg `cache_model_variance_precondition_stddev`) emits this fail-closed bundle when the gate is set and the input stddev falls below the floor. The `predictor_l1_capacity_invalid` reason fires when the L1 head's set-associative refinement detects geometry that is PRESENT but invalid (e.g., a static-card entry's `l1_ways=0`, or an overlarge `l1_ways` value whose derived `set_count < 1` against the cell's effective capacity); a silent fall-through to the fully-associative scalar bundle would mask a malformed `l1_ways` edit during way-count tuning, so the L1 head fails closed instead. The `launch_parameters_sidecar_identity_mismatch` reason fires when the per-cell launch-parameter sidecar's embedded identity tuple (arch / slug / shape_point / binary_sha256 / kernel_signature_sha256) does not match the caller's admitted-row / manifest tuple, OR when the sidecar's `grid_dim` payload is malformed; the producer-side semantic-binding contract requires every predictor input that influences the bundle output to be content-bound to the caller identity, and a stale-or-swapped sidecar would silently apply the wrong gridDim correction otherwise.

headline_validity_failed_reasons.description: Optional list of typed reasons explaining why the bundle's headline value (predicted_hit_rate / hit_rate_lower) is not load-bearing for downstream consumers. Today the only admitted value is `calibration_variance_precondition_failed`; future additive reasons land in lockstep with the verifier + comparison_bundle schema. The field SHOULD be present on every typed-unavailable bundle whose `typed_reason` is the corresponding headline-validity failure; otherwise omitted. Adding entries here does NOT bump schema_version (additive widening per the wire-extension policy).

l1tex_capacity_bytes.description: Per-SM L1 cache capacity in bytes used by the L1 predictor head's per-SM fully-associative walker. Optional on legacy bundles; populated by every bundle that carries an L1-layer prediction. The plan's no-hard-coded-capacity discipline: no L1 capacity constant is hard-coded into implementation or tests; every fixture sources from a manifest, a CUDA-attribute query stub, or the published static-card table at tools/cache_predictor/l1_static_card_table.json. The provenance is recorded in l1tex_capacity_source; a bundle missing l1tex_capacity_source when this field is present is rejected by the conditional schema arm below.

l1tex_capacity_source.description: Closed-enum provenance label for l1tex_capacity_bytes. `device_properties_manifest` = sourced from a manifest entry; `cuda_func_attribute_query` = sourced from a live cuFuncGetAttribute query at predict time; `cuda_device_attribute_query` = sourced from a live cuDeviceGetAttribute query; `static_card_constant` = sourced from the published static-card table. When this enum is `static_card_constant`, the bundle MUST reference an arch that exists in the static-card table (the rejection lives in the predictor's runtime gate, not the schema, because the table is data not schema).

l1_shared_carveout_source.description: Closed-enum provenance label for the shared-memory carveout policy that determines how much of the unified L1 / shared memory budget is allocated to L1. `device_properties_manifest` = sourced from a manifest entry; `cuda_func_attribute` = sourced from a per-kernel cudaFuncAttribute query; `default` = the toolkit's default carveout (lowest fidelity, used only when neither manifest nor per-kernel attribute is available).

static_shared_bytes.description: Statically-allocated shared-memory bytes for the kernel. Subtracts from the unified L1 / shared budget when the carveout policy maps the requested shared size to an L1 capacity bucket. Sourced from the kernel proto's static-shared metadata when available; 0 when the kernel has no static shared region.

dynamic_shared_bytes.description: Dynamically-allocated shared-memory bytes for the kernel (from the launch's `extern __shared__` parameter). Subtracts from the unified L1 / shared budget alongside static_shared_bytes. Sourced from the kernel proto's dynamic-shared metadata; 0 when the kernel does not request dynamic shared.

l1_model_class.description: Closed-enum classifier for the L1 model the per-SM walker applies. (a) `fully_associative_baseline` is the Plan 1 default: a single per-SM LRU over `capacity_bytes / 128` lines; allowed to emit scalar predictions. (b) `set_associative_refinement` is the DEC-2 model: per-(SM, set) LRU stacks each capped at `ways` lines, with set_index = line_id % set_count; sourced from the static-card table's `l1_ways` field (sm_86 records `l1_ways=4`); allowed to emit scalar predictions; the bundle's evidence block records the FA walker's hit/miss counts under `set_associative_refinement_diagnostics` for A/B comparison. (c) `set_associative_refinement_pending` is the deferral marker for arches whose set/way geometry has not yet been sourced; MUST NOT emit scalar (enforced by the `allOf-if` conditional arm in this schema). (d) `reduction_kernel_aware_correction` is the alternative-model-class lever that applies a multiplicative correction to the FA/SA scalar when the predictor-side slug classifier identifies a reduction/activation kernel (suffix `_bf16_sm80` matches layernorm/rmsnorm/silu/softmax in the current sm_86 cohort); the corrected scalar is emitted as `predicted_hit_rate` and the FA/SA result is preserved under `evidence.predicted_l1_hit_rate_uncorrected`. Allowed to emit scalar predictions. The correction factor and classifier metadata are recorded in the evidence block so an auditor can re-verify the correction provenance.

cta_to_sm_schedule_policy.description: Closed-enum CTA-to-SM scheduling policy used by the per-SM L1 walker to distribute blocks across SMs. `round_robin_homogeneous` = block_index modulo sm_count; `occupancy_derived` = caller supplies a per-block sm_id mapping; `unknown` = scheduling metadata is unavailable, in which case the L1 head emits typed_unavailable with reason `predictor_l1_cta_to_sm_schedule_unknown` (guessing the policy biases the prediction because CTAs on different SMs do not evict each other's L1 lines on Ampere / Blackwell baseline).

cache_layer.description: Closed-enum cache-layer classifier. L1TEX denotes a bundle produced by the L1 predictor head (per-SM fully-associative walker over SASS-grounded l1_eligible accesses). L2 denotes a bundle produced by the L2 Smith-Eklund stack-distance predictor head. The producer emits ONE bundle per (cell, cache_layer) pair; the comparison runner's 8-tuple join uses this field as the 8th element so per-layer bundles join independently against the same admitted-cell row (the layer-aware ground-truth resolution reads cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector_pct for L1TEX vs cache_hit_rate_l2_sector_pct for L2). The field is OPTIONAL on the schema for backward compatibility with committed legacy bundles that pre-date the layer-aware migration; those legacy bundles are treated as cache_layer=L2 by the comparison runner. New producer paths emit this field explicitly.

evidence.description: Free-form per-arm evidence payload. For result_kind == 'scalar', may include per-bin admitted hit rates and observation counts. For result_kind == 'typed_unavailable', may include the underlying provenance values (e.g., sector_stream length, bin sample-count vector). The verifier does not validate the inner shape; this is operator-readable diagnostics. The only typed property pinned today is `cross_launch_state_carryover_applied_launch_count`; other fields stay free-form per `additionalProperties: true` so future diagnostic additions do not require a schema bump.

cross_launch_state_carryover_applied_lau.description: Walker-side build-diagnostic counter from `tools/hrd_profiler/observation_builder.py::build_launches_from_trace_dir`. Counts how many launches actually received a non-None inbound LRU state from a prior launch's surviving sectors (i.e., second-and-later launches in a stream when `cross_launch_state_carryover=True`). Stays 0 on cold-start, on first-launch-of-stream paths, and when carryover is disabled. The bundle-provenance scanner at `tools/sm_86_predictor_accuracy_recovery/test_bundle_provenance_scanner.py` requires this >= 1 (alongside `launch_count >= 2`) when the top-level `cache_model_cross_launch_state_carryover` flag is true; absence or zero with carryover-true triggers the fail-closed `bundle_carryover_provenance_mismatch_multi_launch_not_applied` defect. Integer-only contract: a string value would mask producer-side type bugs that the scanner's integer check at line 124 cannot catch.

raw_prediction.description: Smith-Eklund walker's per-launch arithmetic-mean hit rate BEFORE any multiplicative correction. Pulled from evidence.predicted_hit_rate_uncorrected. Monotonic constraint sign +1: a higher uncorrected walker output should yield a higher calibrated prediction, all else equal.

footprint_ratio.description: (unique_sector_count * sector_size_bytes) / cache_model_capacity_bytes. Values >= 1 mean the unique working set exceeds modeled cache capacity; values >> 1 are the high-footprint signature. Monotonic constraint sign -1: larger footprint relative to capacity reduces the calibrated hit rate.

long_rd_tail_mass.description: Fraction of sector-layer reuse-distance observations whose rd_sector_units_min is at or above 4096 sectors (the long-RD threshold matching the L2 high-footprint signature predicate). Monotonic constraint sign -1: more mass in the long-RD tail reduces the calibrated hit rate.

intra_lane_reuse.description: sharing_locality.grounded[class_name=intra_lane].fraction. Lane-local reuse fraction in [0, 1]. Monotonic constraint sign +1: more lane-local reuse increases the calibrated hit rate.

global_share.description: Fraction of sector_stream records whose memory_op_class is GLOBAL. Monotonic constraint sign 0 (unconstrained) -- the active-path head admits global_share as a covariate without a directional prior.

gridDim_density.description: grid_volume / sm_count_for_device. Per-SM CTA oversubscription density in [0, large]. Monotonic constraint sign -1: more oversubscription increases concurrent L2 contention and reduces the calibrated hit rate.

canonical_pre_calibration_features.description: 6-feature canonical pre-calibration block consumed by the monotonic calibration head's active path. Additive optional widening per the wire-extension policy (BL-20260526-schema-additionalproperties-false-requires-lockstep-extension): legacy bundles emitted before this field landed continue to validate. When the block IS present, all 6 fields are required and range-checked. The active path's consumer-side enforcement (workloads/simbench_bw/canonical_features.py::predict_active_path) raises ValueError when the block is absent on a bundle the head needs to score; the schema does NOT make the block REQUIRED at the top-level because that would gratuitously break historical bundles still consumed by the v4 evaluation pipeline. Producer-side: workloads/simbench_bw/canonical_features.py::assemble_canonical_features is the canonical source for emitting the block.

oneOf.description: Scalar arm forbids typed_reason / hit_rate_lower / hit_rate_upper. The admitted scalar arm requires input_sidecar_digests.sector_stream to be present (non-circular witness contract); the typed_unavailable arm may omit it (e.g. for typed_reason=sector_stream_input_missing).

Bounded arm forbids typed_reason / predicted_hit_rate / ci_low / ci_high / ci_half_width. The admitted bounded arm requires input_sidecar_digests.sector_stream to be present (non-circular witness contract).
Typed-unavailable arm forbids any numeric prediction or CI fields.

allOf.description: L1 capacity provenance conditional: when l1tex_capacity_bytes is present on the bundle, l1tex_capacity_source MUST also be present so the consumer can audit where the capacity value came from (manifest / query / static-card table). Without provenance, a future operator cannot tell whether the capacity was sourced from a load-bearing surface or from a stale constant. The plan explicitly forbids hard-coded L1 capacity in implementation or tests; this schema arm is the wire-boundary enforcement.

L1 model-class scalar-rejection conditional: when l1_model_class=set_associative_refinement_pending, the bundle MUST NOT emit a scalar result_kind. The set-associative refinement is a follow-up model; the refinement-pending class is the marker that the model is not yet usable for scalar predictions and the bundle should emit typed_unavailable or bounded instead. The fully_associative_baseline class is the Plan 1 default and IS allowed to emit scalar predictions.
